title: Subsidiary data handoffs and log redaction - Lighthouse Insurance discovery
next_steps: Redwood to share SOC2 + DPA and EU-only hosting options (Maya) - by 2026-09-13
Schedule technical deep dive with Platform and Security (Carlos/Hannah + Tom/Raj) - target week of 2026-09-20
Set up dedicated EU trial environment and sample ingestion for redaction test - Maya to propose POA
action_items: Maya Patel - Send SOC2 report, DPA and subprocessor list - 2026-09-13
Carlos Ruiz - Draft test plan for log redaction and KMS integration - 2026-09-17
Tom Becker - Provide sample event schema and list of PII/PHI fields for redaction - 2026-09-15
summary: Discovery with Lighthouse Insurance exploring Redwood hosted vs Dedicated vs Private for cross-border subsidiary data flows. Primary concerns: audit logs, log retention and redaction, KMS/HSM control, SCCs/data transfer, HIPAA-type PHI handling for certain products, and ability to run an EU-only dedicated trial for latency and legal review.
topics: Private vs Dedicated vs Hosted tradeoffs
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. We're on the calendar for 45 minutes, I see a full panel from Lighthouse — hi all.
[00:08] Evelyn Hart: Hi Maya, thanks, yes we've got Raj, Sofia, Tom, and Ines on. Appreciate you fitting us in.
[00:14] Maya Patel: Great, quick round, I'm Maya, AE on Redwood, Carlos (SE) and Hannah (S E) joining to cover technical details.
[00:21] Carlos Ruiz: hi all, glad to be here.
[00:23] [00:30] Evelyn Hart: To set context, Lighthouse has a handful of EU subsidiaries and a US holding company. We're exploring LLM features for claims triage and internal docs. Main constraints are: EU data residency for EU customers, log retention rules from our regulator, and redaction of PHI in some products.
[00:44] Raj Malhotra: And we need to be able to prove where data lives, who had access, and demonstrate proper key management with HSMs preferably. Also we have to limit cross-border handoffs between subsidiaries unless SCCs are in place.
[00:57] Maya Patel: Understood. That's common. Quick question — are you leaning toward a hosted API or would you prefer dedicated/private right away?
[01:04] Sofia Klein: Our compliance team is nervous about hosted because of subprocessors and data flows. If Redwood can guarantee EU-only residency and provide robust audit logs with redaction controls, we could consider hosted. Otherwise Dedicated in EU or Private would be required.
[01:18] Hannah Lee: To clarify, Redwood Hosted can operate in region-locked model — we can host only in an EU region and limit model routing, but the control plane metadata may still sit in a central control plane unless you opt for private deployment. That said, we do have options for EU-only control plane for enterprise.
[01:34] Tom Becker: When you say "control plane" can you explain what metadata is stored? We can't have claim PHI land in US metadata stores.
[01:42] Carlos Ruiz: Sure — out of the box Redwood stores runtime logs, request metadata for debugging, and aggregated metrics. We can configure what gets persisted. For higher compliance customers we offer redact-at-ingest, and masked logs. But full private deployment gives you full control over the control plane and logs.
[02:00] [02:12] Raj Malhotra: Masked logs sounds promising. Do you support field-level redaction? We have schema with claimant name, SSN equivalent, medical notes — those need deterministic redaction or tokenization.
[02:22] Hannah Lee: Yes we support configurable redaction rules; you can supply regex or schema fields to be redacted before persistence. The runtime can also support prefix caching while keeping the full KV cache ephemeral and not logged. Note: some transcription may say K V cache as "K V" but it's KV.
[02:40] Evelyn Hart: Great. Our legal team also needs to see DPA and subprocessor list and confirmation on SCCs for EU -> US flows.
[02:48] Maya Patel: We'll share the DPA and current subprocessor list. On SCCs, Redwood uses standard EU SCCs and we can append the DPA. If you're doing cross-border fallbacks, we can route to EU-only fallback models — routing policies are configurable.
[03:02] [03:20] Sofia Klein: Another point — audit logs retention requirements differ across countries. Some regulators want seven years, others three. Can retention be per-tenant or per-route?
[03:30] Carlos Ruiz: Retention is configurable per-tenant and per-route. You can set separate retention windows for raw transcripts, structured logs, and metrics. We also support secure erasure workflows for data deletion requests.
[03:44] Raj Malhotra: That's helpful. For key management, does Redwood integrate with our KMS or require Redwood-managed keys?
[03:52] Hannah Lee: Options: Redwood-managed keys for hosted customers; for Dedicated/Private you can bring-your-own KMS — integrations with AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure KeyVault, and HSMs via KMIP. If you need hardware-backed keys, Private deploy with HSM is recommended.
[04:07] Tom Becker: If we bring our own KMS, will Redwood ever escrow keys or have access?
[04:12] Carlos Ruiz: With BYOK in Dedicated/Private, Redwood never has the plaintext keys. We only store key identifiers and use cryptographic operations via KMS APIs/HSM. We can detail the exact call flows in a security review.
[04:22] [04:40] Ines Duarte: One of our thorny concerns is subsidiary handoffs — e.g., a claim starts in Germany, then underwriting in UK, then a repo team in US. How do we ensure the data isn't routed outside of allowed jurisdictions during inference and in caching?
[04:54] Maya Patel: Two levers: region constraint on runtime + smart routing policy. You can pin requests to run only in EU region, and disable cross-region KV cache replication. Also can configure model variant fallback policies to only use EU-hosted model variants.
[05:10] Raj Malhotra: Is there any telemetry that still crosses borders for monitoring? We need to provide an architecture diagram showing nothing leaves the EU.
[05:18] Hannah Lee: For hosted controlled region, some aggregated telemetry might hit central monitoring but we can offer an enterprise package that keeps telemetry in-region or pushes metrics to your Prometheus via a VPC peering. For strict "nothing leaves" we recommend Private or VPC Private offering.
[05:32] [05:50] Evelyn Hart: Let's talk about logs — we need both evidence of access (who queried what), and the content redaction. If a claims handler asks a question that includes PHI, the content should not be stored. Do you support redaction before any persistent logging?
[06:03] Carlos Ruiz: Yes, redact-at-ingest is supported — the runtime can apply rules to drop or mask fields before logging. Also a scrub pipeline can apply secondary redaction to stored logs. Caveat: redaction rules are only as good as the schema; free-form text can leak PHI unless you use regex or a small model-based PII detector.
[06:22] Sofia Klein: Model-based PII detector — that adds complexity. How accurate is it and does it itself need residency guarantees?
[06:30] Hannah Lee: Good callout. If you run the PII-detector in-region (we can set that up in EU trial), detection and redaction never leave the region. The detector can run as a preprocessor in your deployment.
[06:42] [06:55] Tom Becker: We need an experiment: ingest synthetic claims with PHI fields and prove redaction and retention. Can Redwood provide a dedicated EU environment for that?
[07:01] Maya Patel: Yes — we can spin up a dedicated EU trial environment for 30 days for proof-of-concept, including a separate tenant with EU-only routing and BYOK support. We'll propose the POA.
[07:12] Raj Malhotra: Trial sounds good. On licensing — are there cost differences between hosted EU region and Dedicated?
[07:20] Maya Patel: Hosted is usage-based, typically lowest start cost. Dedicated has reservation/commit and predictable throughput; Private has licensing + infra. We'll send a cost comparison.
[07:30] [07:45] Evelyn Hart: Another regulator ask: tamper-evident audit logs with append-only storage. Can Redwood do that?
[07:52] Carlos Ruiz: Yes, we support write-once storage options for audit logs via immutable buckets and chain-of-custody metadata; we can also provide signed log digests if you need additional proof.
[08:03] Sofia Klein: And what about redaction proofs — can we show that a field was redacted at time T and what rule applied?
[08:11] Hannah Lee: You can store audit metadata that records redaction decisions — rule id, timestamp, operator — without storing the original sensitive content. That provides an audit trail without leaking PHI.
[08:23] [08:40] Raj Malhotra: Encryption in transit and at rest is obvious, but do you support customer-managed TLS certs for endpoint ingress?
[08:48] Carlos Ruiz: For Dedicated/Private yes; hosted supports mutual TLS and can also allow custom certs for enterprise routes through an ingress gateway.
[08:58] Ines Duarte: We also have an internal policy that model outputs that contain PHI must not be indexed in search. Is there a way to stop indexing of certain outputs?
[09:07] Maya Patel: Yes — outputs routing and indexing can be controlled. You can set flags on responses that prevent them from entering search indexes or long-term logs.
[09:16] [09:35] Sofia Klein: Switching to legal — we need the DPA and any certifications. Which certifications do you have?
[09:41] Maya Patel: Redwood has SOC 2 Type II. We're working on ISO 27001 scopes for some regions; we have data processing addendum templates and can share a subprocessor list. We'll attach SOC2 and DPA in follow up.
[09:55] Raj Malhotra: Do you perform penetration tests and can we see the pentest summary?
[09:59] Carlos Ruiz: Yes, we conduct annual penetration tests and external audits. We'll share an executive summary and remediation tracker; for detailed reports we usually require an NDA.
[10:10] [10:30] Tom Becker: On the technical integration side, how do we handle user identity and RBAC? We want SSO, SCIM provisioning, and fine-grained role controls.
[10:40] Hannah Lee: Redwood supports SSO via SAML/OIDC, SCIM for provisioning, and granular RBAC. We can map roles to routes and to log access.
[10:50] Evelyn Hart: Ok, good. A few quick scenario questions: 1) If an EU user sends data and the model chooses to call a tool in US-based infra, is that something we can block?
[11:02] Carlos Ruiz: Yes, you can configure tool-calling policies by region and tenant. You can block any outbound tool calls or allow only in-region tool endpoints.
[11:12] [11:30] Maya Patel: We're near halfway through; any open red flags so far from compliance?
[11:36] Sofia Klein: Two: need proof that redaction happens before persistence, and need the DPA + SCC confirmation. Also want a trial in EU with BYOK.
[11:46] Maya Patel: All doable. We'll provide docs and spin up a trial.
[11:51] [12:10] Raj Malhotra: One more — log retention removal: if a regulator requires deletion, can you guarantee ephemerality for certain data and how fast is deletion?
[12:20] Hannah Lee: Deletion can be immediate but propagation depends on retention tier; for audit logs with immutable storage we provide an erase token that marks a record as logically deleted and we can zero out content in shorter windows. We'll document RTO for deletions per tier.
[12:35] Tom Becker: Are there additional charges for immutable storage or signed log digests?
[12:40] Maya Patel: Yes, those are add-ons — we'll put pricing in the follow-up.
[12:50] [13:10] Ines Duarte: For the PII detector, can the detection model be tuned to our domain? We have insurance-specific terms that sometimes confuse off-the-shelf detectors.
[13:20] Carlos Ruiz: You can provide labeled prompts or rules; we can also run a lightweight fine-tune/instruction set tuned on synthetic data. For strict compliance we recommend rule + model hybrid.
[13:32] Sofia Klein: Last thing: regulator wants to know about subprocessors — specifically any cloud provider used for backups or long-term logs and their region footprints.
[13:44] Maya Patel: We'll send the subprocessor list; backups can be region-restricted and we can use customer-managed buckets for long-term logs.
[13:52] [14:10] Raj Malhotra: Alright, next steps — can we recap?
[14:15] Maya Patel: Sure. Action list: I will share SOC2, DPA, subprocessor list and EU-only hosting options by 2026-09-13. Carlos will draft a redaction + test plan by 2026-09-17. Tom will supply sample schemas by 2026-09-15. We'll schedule a technical deep dive the week of 2026-09-20. We'll also propose a 30-day EU dedicated trial and a POA for BYOK/HSM for Private.
[14:41] Sofia Klein: That timeline works for legal.
[14:44] Evelyn Hart: Thanks everyone. We'll review the docs and circle back.
[14:49] Maya Patel: Thanks all — we'll follow up with the deck and docs.
[14:53] [15:00] Meeting ended.

Notes on transcript: occasional transcription errors: "HSM" sometimes transcribed as "H S M", "KV cache" as "K V cache"; proper nouns may be slightly off. There were brief crosstalk moments between Raj and Tom.
